expectations.text: Names the FOSS Contributor Fund as the published method and attributes it to Duane O'Brien and Mandy Grover, Investing in Open Source: The FOSS Contributor Fund, O'Reilly, 2021
expectations.evidence: "the reference model for this kind of fund (the FOSS Contributor Fund, O'Brien & Grover, O'Reilly 2021 — Ambrose's \"$8,000/month, one project a month\" design is a close variant of that model's own $10,000/month reference implementation)"

expectations.text: Opens nominations to everyone with no prerequisite
expectations.evidence: "**Anyone can nominate**, no prerequisite. Restricting nominations to people with linked accounts measurably suppresses turnout — don't do it."

expectations.text: Restricts voting to employees who made an open-source contribution during that voting cycle, and explains the franchise is earned by contributing
expectations.evidence: The actual rule adopted is "One Slack poll, single-select, one vote per person... Restrict it to real employee accounts (exclude guests/bots)" — open to all employees. The contribution-gated franchise is only floated as a hypothetical future change: "If that matters later, the fix is cheap: gate voting to anyone who logged one qualifying contribution that cycle, nothing more." It is not the adopted policy.

expectations.text: Rejects the whole-company Slack poll as the voting rule
expectations.evidence: Section 5 explicitly adopts it: "**One Slack poll, single-select, one vote per person.**" The doc even labels this choice "a legitimate choice," not a rejected one: "Whole-company voting is a legitimate choice; just know it trades away that incentive effect..."

expectations.text: Applies four eligibility filters before the ballot: in use by the company, OSI-approved license, has a mechanism to receive funds, and not maintained by an employee
expectations.evidence: "We actually use it... It carries an OSI-approved license... It has a working mechanism to *receive a sponsorship or donation*... It is **not maintained by a current employee.**"

expectations.text: Excludes ferrite-queue under the employee-maintained rule, or requires an explicit published conflict-of-interest exception for it
expectations.evidence: "**ferrite-queue is disqualified.** It fails the fourth filter, and that filter isn't optional colour on top of the model..."

expectations.text: Excludes the subscription-only candidate because the budget pays one-off amounts
expectations.evidence: The transcript excludes it via the donation-mechanism filter and service-vs-sponsorship distinction, not payment cadence: "The support-subscription-only candidate is disqualified, on the third filter. A paid support contract is a commercial services purchase with deliverables attached... not a sponsorship." The fund itself is also explicitly recurring, not one-off: "Recurring by default: a project that wins isn't a one-off gesture..."

expectations.text: Runs the eligibility check before the ballot rather than after it
expectations.evidence: "What we fund — eligibility (checked before a project reaches the ballot, never after)" and "Run the eligibility filters (§2) on every nomination before it's added to the ballot."

expectations.text: Warns that the vote drifts toward projects that already have money, and requires seeding each ballot with underserved candidates drawn from the dependency graph
expectations.evidence: "open voting drifts toward whatever's already well-funded, and a famous framework with a foundation behind it needs your $8,000 far less..." followed by "Add at least 2–3 candidates sourced from the dependency graph itself, favoring ones with thin maintainer counts or no existing sponsor"

expectations.text: Reuses the nomination list internally as an onboarding menu for employees who want somewhere to start contributing
expectations.evidence: "Reuse the ballot as a standing menu: post it somewhere permanent so employees who want to start contributing know where to look."

expectations.text: Requires the fixed per-cycle amount to be paid promptly, because a fund that pays late loses its internal credibility first
expectations.evidence: No statement anywhere in the transcript ties payment promptness to program credibility; Section 9 ("Payment path") only covers invoiced billing setup and fiscal-host routing, with no mention of payment timeliness or credibility risk.

expectations.text: Requires a published eligibility and conflict-of-interest rule plus employee disclosure before the first cycle
expectations.evidence: "The rules below build the fixes in as standing policy, not one-time exceptions, and are meant to be published internally before the first ballot opens," covering eligibility (§2), conflicts of interest (§7), and disclosure (§8).

expectations.text: Asks who administers the cycle and for how many hours a month, treating the fund as a standing job
expectations.evidence: Section 12 only names an owner: "Name one owner (not \"OSPO\" or \"the fund\") who runs the monthly cycle, checks eligibility before each ballot, and answers questions..." — there is no mention of an hours-per-month time commitment anywhere in the document.

expectations.text: Names the FOSS Contributor Fund as the published method and attributes it to Duane O'Brien and Mandy Grover, Investing in Open Source: The FOSS Contributor Fund, O'Reilly, 2021
expectations.evidence: No such attribution or named source appears anywhere in the document.
